_comment: CLAY, STAGE ONE (#115). Grog IS crushed potsherds - the vanilla item and the real material are
the same noun, so the recipe needs no explaining.
The issue says Separator; it predates the machine split and #189's table lists 'pottery sherd to
grog' under the Pulverizer. Crushing changes only how fine the material is, which is the mill's
verb, not the shredder's.
THE TAG, not twenty-three recipes. #minecraft:decorated_pot_sherds carries all of them, so a
sherd added by a future version or a pack is covered without a mod release - and every sherd
crushes the same, because the picture does not survive being ground.
COUNT IS 1, AND WITH A TAG INPUT IT HAS TO BE. The machine matches per SLOT, and the 23 sherds do
not stack with each other - so count 2 would mean two of the SAME sherd, not two sherds. Fed nine
different ones a mill would fill every slot, mill none of them, and refuse new material until the
player happened to find a duplicate. The stall comment in PulverizerBlockEntity assumes a
single-item input topping itself up, which a multi-item tag never does.
deliberate: the 23 are archaeological designs from trail and ocean ruins, and a household dump
holding the complete set would read as a museum. A sherd obtained any other way still crushes.
THE RECIPE TAKES THE WHOLE TAG while the dump supplies exactly ONE type (owner, 2026-08-17).
Sherds do not stack with each other, so several types means several inventory slots holding what is
functionally one material - the same stacking fact that forced count to 1. One type stacks with
itself and reads as the same broken crockery turning up again, which is what a dump is. A sherd
obtained any other way, or added by a pack, still crushes.
